subject.title: feat(talk/realtime): voice chat should behave identically to text chat — context parity for agent-consult sessions

question: Should realtime Talk agent-consult sessions inherit the canonical text-agent context, and if so should that be unconditional or an explicitly configured privacy boundary?
rationale: The request changes how personal memory and conversation state are exposed to a realtime voice path, which needs an intentional product and privacy contract before implementation.

options.title: Reuse canonical agent context
options.body: Make voice consults use the same established agent-context assembly as text chat, with session ownership and privacy behavior defined centrally.

options.title: Add opt-in voice context
options.body: Expose an explicit Talk setting only if maintainers want voice context to remain separately controlled from normal chat.

options.title: Preserve isolation
options.body: Keep consult sessions isolated and document the distinction if realtime voice must not receive personal context by default.

recommendation.title: Reuse canonical agent context
recommendation.body: Make voice consults use the same established agent-context assembly as text chat, with session ownership and privacy behavior defined centrally.

likelyOwner.reason: Current feature history was not available to route this design decision to a named contributor.
